title: Keep the seat license to one instance per process

blocks.text: The product is sold for 25 concurrent seats, and `SeatLicense` counts them: one instance per process, reached through `getInstance()`. A seat audit found customers using more seats than they paid for, and two `SeatLicense` objects in one process on two occasions. The first appeared at start-up, when the plugin framework instantiated every class of the package through its private constructor before anything had called `getInstance()`. The second appeared after the session store wrote a user's session out and read it back.

items: `checkConstruction()`, which the constructor runs every time, whoever calls it;
`readResolve()`, for a license that is read back from a session.

blocks.text: When you're done, neither the framework nor the session store can produce a second license, and a session read back counts against the live license, with the seats that are claimed now. About four lines in total.
The tests load the class afresh for each test, so each one starts in a process where nothing has used the license yet.

cases.says: getInstance() returns one license that counts all 25 seats, whoever claims them
a reflective call to the private constructor is refused even before getInstance() has run, and getInstance() still works afterwards
reading a written license back gives the instance getInstance() returns
reading a license back leaves the live seat count as it is, not as it was when written

origin.section: Deserialization Makes a Second Instance Without Running the Constructor

concepts: Reading a serialized singleton builds a new object without running its constructor, so the constructor guard never sees it, and the copy carries the state it was written with.
A constructor guard refuses a reflective call only if it reads a field that is already set when the call can happen: the static final instance (or a holder's field), not a lazily set field or a flag.
readResolve returning the instance makes readObject return the live singleton with its live state; what was written is discarded.
setAccessible(true) lets any class-path code call a singleton's private constructor and get a second instance with fresh state.
